The Angular 19 app is built in `/private/tmp/dsb-eval/opus-5-5/A-5` and runs with `npx @angular/cli@19 serve`. Logging in with `admin` / `admin` reaches the dashboard. The production build passes with no warnings.

**How I checked it:** I scripted a headless-browser test against the dev server, covering:
- Empty login submit shows both field errors; a valid login sets `isLoggedIn` and redirects.
- Log lines are added every 3 s.
- The profile menu sits fully inside the 1280 px viewport, opening leftward, and closes on an outside click.
- The table loads 5 rows.
- Details opens and closes; Edit splits "Jane Doe" into first and last name, and saving updates the row.
- An empty invite shows 4 errors; a valid invite adds a row.
- Edit → "Delete user" opens the confirmation for the same member, and Delete removes the row.
- Clicking the backdrop closes the delete dialog.
- Sign Out returns to `/login`, and visiting `/users` afterwards is redirected to `/login`.
- No console errors throughout.

I also compared screenshots of each screen and dialog against the Figma data.

**Styling:** every colour, spacing step, radius, type size and shadow is a CSS custom property in `src/styles.scss`, with values taken from the Figma file. Buttons and form fields are shared classes, and the badge, avatar and dialog are shared components. No component sets its own colours or sizes. The remaining fixed values are the breakpoints (CSS variables can't be used in media queries), the checkbox tick, and one SVG chevron colour.

**Where the spec and Figma disagreed, I followed the spec's content and Figma's styling:**
- **Login:** the Figma card also has a "Blueprint" title and a divider. I left both out because the spec says to add nothing beyond its seven elements.
- **Dashboard:** I used the spec's eight tiles and values; Figma has seven cards with different numbers. Row 2 holds three cards (Throughput spanning two columns, Health, Data Summary). The extra "System Overview / Last updated" heading comes from Figma. I left out Figma's Peak/Average/Total figures under the chart.
- **Tile labels:** uppercase, as the spec requires. Figma uses sentence case for them.
- **Error Rate trend:** shown in Figma's amber "warning" style rather than red, because Figma draws a rising error rate that way.
- **Table:** Avatar and Name are separate columns, as the spec asks; Figma merges them into one "User" column. The row actions use the spec's emphasis order (Details plain, Edit outlined, Delete red outline); Figma's order and styles differ.
- **Header:** the nav links are Dashboard and Team Members, not Figma's placeholder links. Figma has no logo, so the square logo mark is my own. I didn't include the "Online" tag that appears only on the Figma dashboard header.
- **Footer:** Figma only has a slim bar with the copyright and two legal links. The spec asks for the brand and link columns as well, so the upper part of the footer (columns, link names, tagline) is my own design.

**Not verified against Figma:**
- **Image rendering wasn't available,** so I worked from the design data alone and never saw the frames.
- **Border colours:** the data gives card, login-card and divider borders as pure black, which I read as an export artefact; I used light grey (`#EBEBEB`) instead.
- **Invented with no Figma reference:** the profile menu, error states, hover and focus states, the delete dialog, the log viewer's styling (light monospace panel with coloured INFO/WARN/ERROR), the 160 px chart and 240 px log heights, the responsive breakpoints, and the Inter / JetBrains Mono fonts loaded from Google Fonts.
